stem.en: A coral reef stays in the sea, and nobody carries it away. Why does it still count as a marine resource?

text.en: It can be broken up and sold as building stone.

feedback.en: Breaking up a reef destroys it. It counts while it stays where it is, so selling it as stone is not the reason.

text.en: It is an ocean feature that has real value.

feedback.en: Yes. Marine resources are materials and features of the ocean with intrinsic or economic value, and a reef has both.

text.en: It was built by people to bring visitors.

feedback.en: A reef is not built by people. It is a natural feature, and that is part of why it counts.

text.en: It is the only part of the sea that is alive.

feedback.en: The sea holds a great many living things, so a reef is not the only one.

explanation.en: Marine resources are the materials and features found in oceans that have intrinsic or economic value. A resource need not be carried out of the sea. A reef stays in place, and it is valuable for itself and because visitors come to see it.

hints.en: Does a resource have to be taken out of the sea?
Look at the two words in the meaning: materials and features.
